title: Control flow
description: Compares, flags, and conditional branches in NASM
theory:
### Flags and branches

After arithmetic and many logical operations, the CPU records outcomes in **rFLAGS**:
carry, zero, sign, and overflow matter most for branching. In Intel-syntax NASM,
comparisons are usually written as **`cmp`** (subtract) or **`test`** (bitwise AND
without storing a result), followed by a **conditional jump** such as **`je`**, **`jne`**,
**`jl`**, or **`jg`**. Unconditional flow uses **`jmp`**, and tiny loops often pair
**`dec`/`jnz`** or use **`loop`** when **`rcx`** is your counter.

Think of labels as human-readable addresses: the assembler computes distances for
relative jumps in simple cases, while large jumps still assemble cleanly in 64-bit mode.

### Structured layout with `.data`

Constants and small tables live in **`.data`**; uninitialized scratch space belongs in
**`.bss`**. Keeping read-only text separate from writable memory makes reasoning about
bugs easier and matches how real binaries separate **`.text`**, **`.rodata`**, and **`.data`**.

```nasm
global _start
section .data
    needle: db 7
section .text
_start:
    movzx eax, byte [rel needle]
    cmp eax, 7
    je .eq
    ; ... not equal path ...
.eq:
    ; ... equal path ...
```

### Syscalls still drive observable behavior

Control flow is only useful if it eventually reaches **`syscall`** (or calls routines
that do). When branching around I/O, double-check that every path sets **`rax`**, **`rdi`**,
**`rsi`**, and **`rdx`** consistently before a write, and ends with a well-defined exit.

exercises.title: Pick a branch
exercises.description: If `rax` holds `7`, print `T` else print `F` (single character, no newline), then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    t: db 'T'
    f: db 'F'
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 7
    ; cmp / jmp to pick one byte write of length 1
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `cmp rax, 7` then `je` to a label that points `rsi` at `t`
Reuse one `write` syscall block after choosing `rsi`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    t: db 'T'
    f: db 'F'
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 7
    cmp rax, 7
    lea rsi, [rel f]
    jne skip
    lea rsi, [rel t]
skip:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Count-down loop
exercises.description: Use a loop in `.text` to print exactly three stars `***` (no newline) with three single-character writes or one write of length 3 from a buffer you fill.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .bss
    buf: resb 3
section .text
_start:
    ; store '*' '*' '*' into buf then write syscall rdx=3
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `mov byte [buf], '*'` then bump index in a register
Or place `db '*','*','*'` in `.data` and write once
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    stars: db '*', '*', '*'
    slen equ $ - stars
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, stars
    mov rdx, slen
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Signed compare
exercises.description: If `eax` is **less than** `0` (signed), print `N`, else print `P` (one character, no newline), then exit 0. Initialize `eax` to `-3`.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    n: db 'N'
    p: db 'P'
section .text
_start:
    mov eax, -3
    ; jl vs jge to pick letter
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    n: db 'N'
    p: db 'P'
section .text
_start:
    mov eax, -3
    cmp eax, 0
    lea rsi, [rel p]
    jge pos
    lea rsi, [rel n]
pos:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Unsigned compare
exercises.description: Set `rbx` to `10`. If `rbx` equals `10`, print `Y`, else print `N` (one character, no newline), then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    y: db 'Y'
    n: db 'N'
section .text
_start:
    mov rbx, 10
    ; cmp rbx, 10 then pick y or n
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    y: db 'Y'
    n: db 'N'
section .text
_start:
    mov rbx, 10
    cmp rbx, 10
    lea rsi, [rel n]
    jne skip
    lea rsi, [rel y]
skip:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
